ruleset.name: DeclaredAccessMode
ruleset.description: Apex database operations must declare their access mode. From API version 67.0 an operation without a declared mode runs in user mode, so automation fails silently for a running user without field access; up to API version 66.0 the default is system mode. Declaring the mode keeps the behavior explicit across API versions. Test classes and test data factories (class name containing "TestFactory") are not checked.

rule.name: SoqlWithoutAccessMode
rule.message: SOQL query without a declared access mode. Use WITH SYSTEM_MODE in automation (trigger, event, job) and WITH USER_MODE in screen controllers.
rule.description: Flags static SOQL without WITH SYSTEM_MODE, WITH USER_MODE or WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED.

rule.name: DatabaseCallWithoutAccessLevel
rule.message: Database method without AccessLevel. Pass AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE in automation (trigger, event, job) and AccessLevel.USER_MODE in screen controllers.
rule.description: Flags Database.insert, update, upsert, delete, undelete, merge, query, countQuery and getQueryLocator without an AccessLevel argument. A call that receives static SOQL is left to SoqlWithoutAccessMode, and a dynamic query whose text literal carries WITH SYSTEM_MODE or WITH USER_MODE is accepted. Keyword DML (insert, update) is not checked, because the PMD tree does not tell "insert as system" from a plain insert.
